chunks: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Isma'il al-Sakuni narrated to us in his house in Kufa. He said: Ibrahim b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Nisapuri narrated to me. He said: Abu Ja'far b. al-Siri and Abu Nasr b. Musa b. Ayyub al-Khallal narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Sa'id narrated to us. He said: Damra b. Shawdhab narrated to us from Matar from Shahr b. Hawshab from Abu Hurayra. He said:

Whoever fasts on the eighteenth of Dhul Hijja, Allah records for him the fasting of sixty months; and it is the day of Ghadir Khumm, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the hand of Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and said: "O people! Am I not more of a master over the believers?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "For whomever I am a master, Ali is his master." Then Umar said to him: "Bravo, bravo, O son of Abi Talib! You have become my master and the master of every Muslim." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "This day I have perfected your religion for you" [5:3].

key_terms.أولى بالمؤمنين: More of a master over the believers; referring to the Prophet's authority
key_terms.غدير خم: Ghadir Khumm; a watering hole between Mecca and Medina where the Prophet made his famous declaration
key_terms.مولاه: His master/guardian (mawla); a key term denoting authority, loyalty, and guardianship

ai.seo_question: What happened at Ghadir Khumm and what is the reward for fasting on the 18th of Dhul Hijja?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Abu Hurayra, establishes the event of Ghadir Khumm on the 18th of Dhul Hijja when the Prophet (s) declared Ali b. Abi Talib (as) as the mawla (master/guardian) of every believer. The narration emphasizes three key elements: the immense reward of fasting on this day (equivalent to sixty months), Umar's congratulation of Ali upon the declaration, and the subsequent revelation of Quran 5:3 completing the religion of Islam. For the Shia tradition, this event is the foundational proof of Ali's divinely appointed succession.
